claims.text: Alex Hormozi structured his $100 Million Money Models book launch with two parallel conversion paths: (1) free registration to a live virtual event, and (2) a paid pre-order with four bundled bonuses. The free path lowers the barrier for maximum attendance while the paid path captures committed buyers at the point of highest interest, before the event occurs.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Free registration maximizes audience size by removing all purchase friction; paid pre-order with bonuses converts highest-intent audience before the event, using urgency of the live date as the conversion trigger.
bounded_by: Requires a large existing audience to drive meaningful free registrations
Live event format required to create the time-bound conversion pressure

claims.text: Alex Hormozi deployed a live-only exclusive giveaway (described as more than an NFT and less than a Bitcoin in value) as an attendance incentive for his $100 Million Money Models launch event, explicitly requiring physical live presence to receive it. This mechanism converts passive registrants into active attendees by introducing a non-transferable, time-bound scarcity reward.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: audience already registered or aware of the event
claims.mechanism: A live-only reward that cannot be accessed via replay or registration alone forces attendance decision; the mystery framing amplifies curiosity while the value bracket (more than NFT, less than Bitcoin) anchors perceived worth without revealing specifics.
bounded_by: Requires a genuinely valuable and deliverable live-only reward to avoid perceived manipulation
Does not apply to evergreen on-demand courses where live attendance is not a product feature

claims.text: Alex Hormozi reported that his prior comparable virtual launch event attracted hundreds of thousands of live concurrent attendees and generated enough traffic to nearly crash the hosting infrastructure. This precedent establishes that virtual book launch events at scale can match or exceed in-person conference attendance.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

numbers.axis: live concurrent attendees at virtual book launch events

anchors.value: nearly broke the internet (capacity limit reached)

bounded_by: Speaker self-reported; no independent verification cited
Requires a large pre-existing audience to replicate

claims.text: Alex Hormozi committed to spending millions of dollars on the launch of $100 Million Money Models, treating launch spend as a media and distribution investment rather than a production cost. This signals that at scale, book launch ROI justifies seven-figure marketing budgets because the launch event itself generates revenue (pre-orders, backend offers) rather than functioning purely as a promotional expense.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: existing personal brand with millions of followers
virtual event model with embedded offer stack
book as front-end lead generator for higher-ticket back-end

numbers.axis: launch marketing spend for book launch events

bounded_by: Only justifiable when the launch event itself converts to revenue (pre-orders, backend offers) to offset the spend
Does not apply to first-time authors without audience or offer stack

examples.text: During the announcement for $100 Million Money Models, Alex Hormozi referenced his prior virtual launch event as proof of scale: hundreds of thousands of people attended live, and the infrastructure nearly crashed from the load. He used this precedent to frame the upcoming launch as even larger, citing millions in planned launch spend and a mystery live-only giveaway to drive attendance.

practices.text: For large-scale book or product launches with an existing audience, offer free registration to maximize reach while simultaneously providing a paid pre-order path with bundled bonuses to capture committed buyers before the event date.
Include at least one live-only exclusive benefit in virtual launch events that cannot be accessed via replay or recording, to maximize conversion from registered to attended.
Keep the nature of exclusive live giveaways mysterious but anchor their value with a comparable range (e.g., more than X, less than Y) to maximize curiosity without over-promising.
